what_its_for: Meropenem is a strong antibiotic used to fight serious bacterial infections in your body. It is commonly used to treat infections in your lungs (pneumonia), belly (abdomen), kidneys, urinary tract, skin, and brain (meningitis). It works by stopping the bacteria from building their protective outer wall, which kills them.
how_to_take: This medicine is given directly into your vein (intravenously or IV) by a nurse or healthcare provider in a hospital or clinic setting. You will NOT take this as a pill. The IV infusion is usually given slowly over 15 to 30 minutes, or sometimes over 3 to 4 hours depending on what your doctor ordered. Never try to give this medicine to yourself at home unless a healthcare team has specifically trained you and set up a home infusion program for you.
dosing: Your dose is decided by your doctor based on the type and severity of your infection, your body weight, and how well your kidneys are working. Common adult doses range from 500 mg to 2,000 mg (2 grams) given every 6 to 8 hours. Children's doses are based on their weight. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare provider, missed doses are uncommon. If you are receiving this at home and you miss a dose, give it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up to make up for a missed dose. Call your doctor or home infusion nurse if you are unsure what to do.
storage: The premixed bag of meropenem in saline should be stored in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F / 2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it. Once you take it out of the refrigerator, it can stay at room temperature for up to 4 hours — use it within that time or throw it away. Always check the expiration date on the bag before using it. Keep it away from light and out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because some can interact with meropenem. Specifically, avoid taking valproic acid (Depakote) or valproate while on meropenem, as this antibiotic can make valproic acid stop working, which could trigger seizures if you have epilepsy. Avoid skipping doses or stopping treatment early, even if you feel better — finishing the full course is important to cure your infection and prevent antibiotic resistance.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: a skin rash, hives, or itching; swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction); trouble breathing; seizures or uncontrolled shaking; severe or ongoing diarrhea (especially if it is bloody or watery — this could be a dangerous gut infection called C. difficile); yellowing of your skin or eyes; dark urine or unusual tiredness (signs of liver problems); or pain, redness, or swelling at your IV site.
when_it_works: Most patients start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting treatment. However, it is very important to complete your full course of antibiotics even if you feel well before it is finished. Stopping too soon can allow the infection to come back or become harder to treat. Your doctor will monitor your progress with lab tests and physical check-ups.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If your kidneys do not work well, your doctor will lower your dose or space out your doses to prevent the medicine from building up to harmful levels. Your kidney function will be monitored regularly. Older adults (65+): Older patients may need dose adjustments because kidney function naturally decreases with age. Children: This medicine can be used in children, including newborns, with doses carefully calculated by weight. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits carefully before prescribing this medicine.
